Q1.text: What is your first priority as ruler of the Dwarven Kingdom?

options.text: Invest in reinforced tunnels (strengthen before expanding)
Militarize the guards to secure mines
Push aggressive mining (dig deeper, faster)

Q2.text: You shore up tunnels and invest in infrastructure. Continue?

options.text: Proceed carefully with expansion
Proceed carefully with economy

Q3.text: You deploy guards throughout the mines. Deploy them now?

options.text: Deploy guards across tunnels
Deploy guards at key points

Q4.text: You push miners to work faster and deeper. Continue?

options.text: Order miners to keep digging
Order miners to slow down and focus on safety

Q5.text: Despite reinforcements, a massive underground fault is discovered beneath the capital. How do you respond?

options.text: Exploit it carefully — send elite engineers to mine and study the fault
Seal the fault permanently (close the affected shafts for safety)
Guard and study slowly — secure the area and research it over time

Q6.text: With guards stationed throughout the mines, productivity rises — but the atmosphere grows tense. One night a violent clash breaks out in a tunnel (a guard is killed, the tunnel is sealed). How do you handle the crisis?

options.text: Hold a public trial — investigate and deliver justice openly
Enforce harsh military justice — make an example of the miners
Reduce military presence and restore civilian oversight

Q9.text: The mining team leader asks: 'What has keys but opens no locks, space but no room, and can enter but cannot go?' (Answer: a keyboard)

Q10.text: The sealing team's riddle: 'I am taken from a mine and shut in a wooden case, yet I am used by those who never see me. Kings have killed for me, but I have no value to the dead. The more of me you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?'

Q11.text: The research team's puzzle: 'The more you remove from me, the larger I become. Engineers curse me; strategists exploit me. What am I?'

Q12.text: The court's question: 'What binds a community more surely than law yet cannot be seen?' (Hint: 5 letters)

Q13.text: The engineers ask: 'What must you name to prevent collapse, that stands when pushed, but falls when neglected?' (1 word)

Q14.text: After addressing the fault and recent unrest, you must set long-term policy. Which will you choose?

options.text: Invest in living conditions (build rest halls and housing for miners)
Support industry — prioritize output over welfare

Q15.text: Diplomat's Trial: 'I end wars without fighting, build bridges without stone, and vanish the moment pride speaks louder. Name me' (1 word)

Q16.text: A new opportunity appears: a rich vein discovered near the sealed fault. How do you act?

options.text: Exploit it carefully using the lessons learned
Force extraction immediately to reap rewards

Q17.text: EVENT 3: The Dwarven Doctrine — With the immediate crisis resolved, the council gathers to define the Dwarven way forward. What defines the dwarven path?

options.text: Wealth and Trade — Turn the mountain into a trade empire.
Craftsmanship Above All — Focus on builders, engineers, and artisans.
Fortress of Stone — Prepare for war and maintain massive defenses.
Regulate Foreign Presence — Manage trade and foreign merchants carefully.

Q18.text: Wealth and Trade — Markets expand rapidly, but foreign merchants gain influence inside dwarven cities. How do you respond?

options.text: Regulate foreign presence (tight rules and oversight)
Tax foreign merchants heavily to fill the treasury
Let prosperity run its course (minimal intervention)

Q19.text: Craftsmanship Above All — You prioritize artisans, guilds, and design. Do you open guild knowledge to outsiders?

options.text: Share selected knowledge for profit and alliances
Guard dwarven secrets — remain unrivaled but isolated

Q20.text: Fortress of Stone → The Living Fortress is completed. Maintaining it drains resources. Your command?

options.text: Boost military spending to keep defenses immaculate
Convert parts of the fortress to civic uses to reduce cost (dual-use structures)

Q21.text: Regulate Foreign Presence — A delegation from the surface asks for access. How will you proceed?

options.text: Offer limited trade licenses under royal permission
Strengthen diplomatic oversight — tighter rules and monitoring
Nationalize key assets — bring foreign-owned infrastructure under state control

Q23.text: Tax Foreign Merchants Heavily — The treasury swells but whispers spread. How do you allocate and manage the revenue?

options.text: Use taxes to fund state expansion (infrastructure and projects)
Increase tax enforcement to squeeze more revenue from merchants
Offer tax relief in exchange for demonstrated loyalty
Share knowledge for profit (sell blueprints, open workshops)
Open the Royal Reserves to buy materials for the people

Q24.text: Market master's riddle: 'I grow when left alone, shrink when controlled too much. I am the tide that lifts all boats, but also drowns the unwary. What am I?'

Q25.text: I am the invisible chain that guides the visible hand. I am the framework within which freedom dances. Too loose, and chaos reigns; too tight, and progress suffocates. What am I?'

Q26.text: I am the only thing you can keep after giving it to someone else. I cannot be bought, but can be stolen. I have no value until given away. Once lost, I can never be found. What am I?'

Q33.text: I can be sold but never bought, shared but never halved. The more you give me away, the more powerful you become. What am I?'

Q36.text: The council's decision defines the Dwarven Doctrine for this era. Proceed to the Final Trial or investigate a newly reported rich vein?

options.text: Proceed to the Final Trial (riddles)
Investigate the rich vein before the Trial

Q40.text: Convert Defenses into Dual-Use Structures — Walls become living spaces, training halls, and markets. How will you adapt the Living Fortress?

options.text: Reduce military spending and repurpose funds
Train a new generation of dwarves (craftsmanship & trade)
Maintain essential maintenance and keep dual-use balance

Q41.text: Reduce Military Spending — Life improves, but defenses weaken slightly. You must allocate the surplus. Where does the money go?

options.text: Invest in Trade Guilds to stimulate commerce
Renovate the Great Hall to restore cultural prestige
Bolster secret intelligence to protect interests cheaply

Q43.text: Train a New Generation of Dwarves — The new smiths must create a final masterpiece for the 'Trial of the Anvil'. Resource shortages force a single approach. How will they prove mastery?

options.text: Refine Ancient Techniques — perfect traditional methods
Mass Production Study — design efficient tools to jumpstart growth
Experimental Alloys — embrace risky innovation with volatile crystals

Q47.text: I am always hungry, I must always be fed. The finger I touch will soon turn red. I devour stone and steel alike, yet a single word can end my strike. What am I?'

Q48.text: I have no voice, yet I speak to you. I have no wings, yet I fly. I have no eyes, yet I weep. I am born in darkness but die in light. The wisest men have drowned in me. What am I?'

Q49.text: I am the only thing that belongs to you but is used more by others. I am the heaviest burden when empty, and the lightest when full. I am the one thing you cannot give away without keeping it. What am I?'

Q50.text: I am older than the mountain, yet renewed with each master. I am taught but never learned, for I live in the hands, not the mind. What am I?'

Q51.text: I turn one into many, effort into ease. I am the child of necessity, the parent of wealth. Without me, progress crawls; with me, it races. What am I?'

Q52.text: I am born in risk and tempered by failure. I break what came before to build what comes next. I am the forge of progress, but also its graveyard. What am I?'

R1.text: I increase when you build nothing, decrease when you build too much, and disappear when you build blindly.'

R2.text: In our city, nothing moves without me, yet no one ever travels on me. When I am misjudged, traffic jams appear underground. What was misjudged?'

R3.text: Water never asks permission. It follows me every time. Build me wrong, and homes flood. Build me right, and no one notices. What am I?'

R4.text: Guards widen me to calm trade. Narrow me, and control becomes easier. I decide who meets whom. What am I?'

R5.text: The Dwarves worshipped ancestors, but feared me more than gods, because I never forgive.'

R6.text: I move slower than armies, faster than laws, and once I start, even kings evacuate.'

R7.text: SimCity rewards me early, punishes me late, and hides my limit completely.'

R8.text: The Dwarves blamed workers for me, generals blamed spies, but engineers blamed time.'

R9.text: I am strongest when invisible, weakest when displayed, and fatal when ignored.'

R10.text: In peace I am a statistic. In war I am a weapon. In collapse I am irrelevant.'

R11.text: The city grew richer every year, yet poorer every decade. I was never taxed.'

R12.text: I increase economy today, decrease health tomorrow, and rewrite history next generation.'

R13.text: The Dwarves sealed me once, and the city survived. They opened me again, and legends were born—or buried.'

R14.text: SimCity lets you pause me, but reality never does. Dwarves respect me more than kings.'

R15.text: I do not exist in maps, only in meetings, yet wars are fought because of me.'

R16.text: The deeper the city went, the smaller I became, until progress stopped entirely.'

R17.text: The council ignored me because I had no voice, but when I finally spoke, the mountain answered.'

R18.text: SimCity calls me a slider. The Dwarves called me a curse. Engineers called me inevitable.'

R19.text: I grow faster than cities, slower than disasters, and never where planned.'

R20.text: When all four stats are high, I decide whether the city lives. When all four are low, I decide whether it dies quietly or violently.'
